title: Chevron Stock Nears a 52-Week High Amid Goldman's Bullish Call: Is CVX Worth Buying Now? - International Business Times, Singapore Edition
content: Chevron stock reached a 52-week high of $225.67 on Monday before closing at $224.37, as Goldman Sachs raised its price target on the energy company to $241 from $228 and maintained a Buy rating. The bank cited Chevron's valuation relative to peers, while investors continue to assess the company's production growth, earnings outlook and exposure to volatile commodity prices. Goldman Sachs revised its earnings-per-share estimates to $17.77 for 2026, $15.27 for 2027, and $13.66 for 2028. The estimates account for changes in commodity prices, refining margins, production costs, and pricing realizations. The bank identified commodity prices, refining margins, and operational execution as key risks to its outlook. Chevron (NYSE: CVX) has gained approximately 51.7% in 2026 through the period covered by the supplied market data. The stock opened the year at $151.67 and closed at $224.99 on Oct. 16, and its reported 52-week low is $146.49. Other Wall Street firms have also raised their targets. Morgan Stanley increased its target to $226 from $218 on Oct. 15, maintaining an Overweight rating. UBS raised its target to $235 from $220 in early October and retained a Buy rating. Piper Sandler has a target of $243. MarketBeat's data lists an average 12-month price target of $213.42 across 28 analysts, with a high of $243 and a low of $90. The average is below Chevron's reported Oct. 19 closing price of $224.37, providing a counterpoint to Goldman's more optimistic assessment. Chevron reported second-quarter 2026 earnings of $12.1 billion, or $6.11 per diluted share, on July 31. Adjusted earnings were $12 billion, or $6.06 per share. Worldwide net oil-equivalent production reached 4.07 million barrels per day, up 20% from a year earlier, according to the company's reported results. Revenue was at $67.2 billion, compared with $44.4 billion in the same quarter of 2025. Production growth included contributions from assets acquired through the Hess transaction and expansion in the Permian Basin. U.S. upstream production reached a record 2.1 million barrels per day. Chevron reported $19.7 billion in cash flow from operations excluding working capital and $15.4 billion in adjusted free cash flow for the quarter. Chevron Chairman and CEO Mike Wirth said in the July 31 earnings call, "Faced with geopolitical uncertainty and market volatility, Chevron's people remain focused on safely delivering the reliable energy the world needs. Our strong second quarter performance is a result of disciplined investment and strong execution that drove record U.S. upstream production, record crude throughput in our U.S. refineries, and exceptional reliability across key assets." Chevron reaffirmed its 2030 targets of 2% to 3% annual production growth and more than 10% free cash flow growth. The company also guided 2026 capital expenditures toward the lower end of its $18 billion to $19 billion range. The supplied data puts Chevron's price-to-earnings ratio at 21.61 and its price-to-earnings-growth ratio at 0.63. Goldman Sachs' valuation assessment suggests the stock is attractively priced relative to its expected growth, but these ratios depend on the share price and earnings estimates used in their calculation. Chevron's dividend yield is 3.17%, and the company has increased its dividend for 38 consecutive years. The yield fluctuates with the share price, and future dividend increases are not guaranteed. The gap between Goldman Sachs' $241 target and the $213.42 analyst consensus highlights the differing expectations for Chevron's future performance. Chevron's third-quarter 2026 results are scheduled for Oct. 23. Investors will be watching production trends, refining performance, cash generation, and management's outlook for the remainder of the year.

content: Chicago, IL – October 20, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: EOG Resources EOG, ExxonMobil Holdings XOM, Diamondback Energy FANG and Chevron CVX. The Permian Basin remains a key driver of U.S. oil production, supported by technological advancements, improving drilling efficiencies and extensive infrastructure. Its proximity to Gulf Coast refining and export facilities further enhances its strategic importance. Leading producers, including EOG Resources, ExxonMobil Holdings, Diamondback Energy and Chevron, continue to strengthen their operations in the region, focusing on production growth, cost reductions and cash flow generation. Spanning West Texas and southeastern New Mexico, the Permian Basin continues to benefit from advances in horizontal drilling, longer laterals and improved well-completion techniques. These developments are enabling operators to boost productivity while maintaining capital discipline. The latest quarterly results from major producers highlight the basin's continued importance to U.S. energy production. EOG Resources continues to perform well in the Delaware Basin, benefiting from faster drilling and improved infrastructure. During the first half of 2026, the company increased its daily drilling activity by 13%, while the length of horizontal wells completed per day rose 5%. These improvements helped lower drilling and completion costs by $15 per foot to less than $710 per foot. EOG's Janus gas processing plant, which can handle 300 million cubic feet of natural gas daily, operated at more than 99% capacity utilization during the first half of the year. The plant also helped the company earn 65 cents more per thousand cubic feet of gas processed. For 2026, EOG expects oil production to grow 5% and total production to increase 14% across its operations. ExxonMobil continues to expand its Permian operations following the acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources. The company's production in the region reached a record of more than 1.8 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the second quarter of 2026. ExxonMobil is using advanced drilling technologies and longer horizontal wells to extract more oil while reducing costs. During the first half of 2026, the company drilled more than 80 wells, each with a horizontal section extending four miles, using real-time monitoring and remote operations to improve efficiency. ExxonMobil aims to increase its Permian production by 9% annually through 2030. Diamondback Energy remains a leading oil producer in the Permian Basin, focusing on reducing costs and improving well productivity. The company has kept drilling, well-completion and equipment costs at approximately $550 per foot in the Midland Basin. Its strategy of developing multiple oil-producing layers helps it recover more resources and improve returns while keeping costs competitive. Diamondback expects to generate approximately $7.8 billion in free cash flow in 2026, supported by its efficient operations and disciplined capital spending. The company has also doubled its share buyback authorization to $16 billion, highlighting its commitment to returning cash to shareholders. Chevron continues to prioritize efficiency and cash flow generation in the Permian Basin after achieving its production milestone of 1 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025. The company reported record Permian production in the second quarter of 2026. Chevron expects capital expenditure per barrel of oil equivalent across its U.S. shale and tight operations to decline 25% in 2026 compared with 2025. The company also achieved $3 billion in annualized structural cost reductions across its business, six months ahead of schedule, reinforcing its emphasis on operational efficiency and capital discipline. The Permian Basin remains central to U.S. oil production, with leading operators focusing on higher recoveries, lower development costs and disciplined investments. EOG Resources, ExxonMobil, Diamondback Energy and Chevron are leveraging their extensive asset positions and operating efficiencies to support production and cash flow, making them important energy stocks for investors to monitor. title: Why Did XOM, CVX, MPC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. XOM stock has gained more than 48% year-to-date, while CVX and MPC stocks have surged more than 47% and 200%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. Combining the drugs raised apoptosis to 36.5% and necrosis to 30.6%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. U.S. stock futures climbed into positive territory late Monday as technology stocks rebounded after a sharp selloff last week. Meanwhile, markets are keenly watching the third-quarter (Q3) earnings season unfold, with about 70 S&P 500 companies slated to report earnings this week. As of 11:13 p.m. EDT, Dow futures were up about 0.25%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.21% and the Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.15%. On Monday, the three benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Nasdaq Composite led the climb, adding more than 290 points to close 1.11% higher. The S&P 500 climbed 0.41% at close, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.07%. Technology and AI stocks were top of mind for markets on Monday as the sector reversed last week's steep selloff. Chip stocks led the climb on Monday. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed up nearly 2%, while the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) closed up 1.61%. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Micron Technology Inc. (MU) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) all ended the session in green. The run comes ahead of vital Q3 results that will follow this week, which are likely to set the tone for the trajectory of technology shares. “Tech earnings are key this week. Fundamentals are unchanged, but given fragile price action, we turn neutral [on] risk assets and stay neutral duration,” Ajay Rajadhyaksha, global chairman of research at Barclays, said in a note, according to CNBC. Katie Stockton, founder of Fairlead Strategies, reportedly said in a note on Monday that the week will be crucial for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which need to hold support, while noting that a hold is possible amid widespread, short-term oversold conditions. Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) are due to report Q3 results later this week, while multiple other semiconductor and technology companies, including Lam Research (LRCX) and Texas Instruments (TXN), will also post their results. AI-related power companies Bloom Energy (BE) and Valero Energy (VLO), along with big entertainment companies including Netflix Inc. (NFLX), will also announce their quarterly results. Meanwhile, rising oil prices amid growing geopolitical uncertainty have put downward pressure on markets. Brent crude futures expiring in December were trading at $109.88 a barrel, up about 0.3%, while WTI crude futures expiring in November traded at $103.64 per barrel. Economist Peter Schiff said in a post on X, “Oil rose another 2.5% today. It's almost $104. If you think gas prices are high now, just wait until after the midterms when Trump has to turn off the spigots from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to keep it from running dry. Oil could hit $150, sending gas prices to record highs.” Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (DJT): Shares of the president’s media company were in focus late Monday after the stock slipped 8%, its worst single-day drop since February, as President Donald Trump’s approval rating hit a record low. Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN): The company’s stock surged nearly 5% at close on Monday and continued to climb higher overnight after Morgan Stanley raised its price target and named it a ‘Top Pick.’ Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS): The AI hardware and supercomputing company was on the retail radar after shares slipped more than 5% on Monday, extending a broader selloff in the sector from last week. CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV): Shares of the neocloud company fell more than 1% in overnight trading late Monday, putting it on track for a third week of declines amid a selloff in software names. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) all climbed overnight. Meanwhile, U.S. long-dated Treasury yields continued above 5%. At the time of writing, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was 5.138%, and the 30-year Treasury yield was 5.473%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.09% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment. Asian markets opened lower on Tuesday, with South Korea's KOSPI, Japan’s Nikkei 225, China’s SSE Composite and Australian stocks all trading lower at the time of writing. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Shares of Broadcom, Inc. (AVGO) reversed overnight losses to edge up 0.3% late Monday as a 10-year cloud agreement with NTT Docomo did little to ease retail skepticism, with traders seeking a recovery catalyst after CEO Hock Tan’s AI “casino” remarks. AVGO stock rose nearly 2% on Monday to close at $334.59, snapping three straight sessions of losses. Broadcom extended its 2019 deal with Docomo, in which the companies will align their long-term tech roadmaps to advance the private cloud underpinning the Japanese telecom operator’s digital services. The company called it Broadcom Japan’s first “comprehensive” 10-year agreement covering VMware software licenses, technical assistance and maintenance support. Financial terms were not disclosed. VMware Cloud Foundation will be at the core of the infrastructure. The deal targets three priorities: keeping services available during system upgrades, strengthening security and resilience, and accelerating the delivery of new services. Docomo will use the platform to expand capacity and manage traffic spikes, improve security patching and anomaly detection, and run virtual machines and containers on a common platform. Automation across development, testing and releases will help shorten the time needed to introduce new features. The companies also plan to expand AI-driven operations and prepare the infrastructure for future developments, including 6G and IOWN. The agreement comes a week after Tan’s comments at a Singapore panel, where he called capital the biggest constraint on further AI development as Broadcom works through wafer and memory shortages. “A lot of investors have no clue what they're investing in, but set very extreme expectations, only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino gambling,” Tan said when asked about cheaper AI models, Reuters noted. His remarks addressed investment into the broader AI sector. Tan also acknowledged that Anthropic and OpenAI had shown an ability to generate significant revenue from their latest models deployed for AI personal assistants. SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk also subsequently responded, saying, “No crying in the casino,” weighing in on Tan’s concerns about speculative AI investments. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for AVGO slipped to ‘extremely bearish’ at 24/100 — its lowest levels in nearly 18 months — from ‘bearish’ levels a day ago amid a 300% surge in 24-hour message volumes. Retail interest in the stock has been rising, with the ticker’s watcher base up 8% over the past three months. One user said, “The biggest problem with this stock is lack Catalysts from Broadcom, the last news was on Oct 13 for VMware HyperArmor. But nothing after it.”  Another user said, “Each time they beat earnings and revenue estimates. Yet here we are down 15% in that time frame.” A separate user said, “trash news! Still headed lower,” shortly after the Docomo agreement. Other traders were still looking for a bounce. Another user said, “when we sell off early into the session typically we see a nice reversal in overnight session into premarket.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. (CRWV) shares fell nearly 2% in overnight trading late Monday, putting it on track for a third week of declines amid a selloff in software names. However, Cathie Wood's ARK Investment purchased 132,498 shares of the company on Monday despite the selloff. The asset manager’s ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) bought 102,280 CRWV shares on Monday for $6.3 million, according to its website. The firm also bought 30,218 shares of CRWV for $1.8 million through the ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). The purchase comes as Wall Street and Main Street remain concerned about the company’s ballooning debt levels. CoreWeave reported $35.6 billion in total debt as of June 30, while its second-quarter net interest expense rose to $640 million from $267 million a year earlier. Research and advisory firm Gartner recently said in a report that artificial intelligence infrastructure investments are in danger as concerns over bloated AI capex mount. The firm said that as the commercial duopoly for primary frontier models consolidates around Anthropic and OpenAI, the cash flows to meet that massive computing asset base from neoclouds are not scaling proportionally with upfront costs. Meanwhile, major Wall Street analysts are also taking opposing stances on CoreWeave. MoffettNathanson and BNP Paribas lowered their price targets on CoreWeave, while Goldman Sachs took a more positive outlook. MoffettNathanson slashed CRWV stock’s target to $89 from $107 and kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares, citing its “staggering financial obligations.” BNP Paribas also cut its price target on CoreWeave to $117 from $169 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm said that it sees a continued deterioration in investor confidence amid its debt obligations. While higher financing costs could contain the company's ability to fund future growth, the shares are "seemingly discounting some liquidity concerns," the analyst reportedly said in a research note. However, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and set a price target of $106, implying upside of more than 73% from its last close. The firm said ongoing volatility in the credit market raises questions about whether CoreWeave can finance its next phase of growth, and at what pace. However, Goldman also said the ongoing debate over demand for frontier vs. off-frontier intelligence, and CoreWeave's annual recurring revenue per megawatt and unlevered internal rate of return, are "biased to the upside" over the next 24 months because of tight supply. The analyst also said that CoreWeave is differentiated from other neoclouds. Last week, Dan Ives, Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director analyst, said in an interview that the recent sell-off was an overreaction, as the broader AI demand story remains intact. “I'm not saying there's not some issues in terms as rates go higher. But given the demand, given backlog, I think this is ultimately a false narrative,” he said, while also highlighting that the sharp drop has created an opportunity for investors. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for CRWV stock was ‘extremely bullish,’ even as message volumes surged 938% over 24 hours, according to platform data. One user said, “$CRWV $NBIS are moving in tandem.. absolutely nothing to see here…” The user added, “When the wrestling match ends, these are going straight up, meanwhile, you or I have zero say in it.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals (EYPT), CoreWeave (CRWV) and Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE) hit fresh 52-week lows Monday as a failed drug trial, debt refinancing concerns, and weaker full-year revenue expectations weighed on the stocks. EyePoint stock crashed 85%, while CoreWeave and Eos Energy stocks dropped 0.4% and 0.5%, respectively. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals stock crashed to a record low of $0.4 after the company reported disappointing results from LUCIA, its second pivotal Phase 3 study of DURAVYU, an experimental treatment for wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The drug failed to show that it worked as well as aflibercept in protecting vision at Weeks 52 and 56, hurting its chances of approval for the eye condition. The setback prompted the company to lay off 53% of its workforce, with the restructuring expected to bring $30 million in annualized savings and incur about $9 million in severance expenses. EyePoint reported roughly $118 million in cash and equivalents as of Sept. 30 and plans to concentrate its remaining resources on Phase 3 studies of DURAVYU for diabetic macular edema (DME). However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bearish’. CoreWeave stock fell to a new annual low of $59.25 as analysts cut price targets amid concerns about its debt obligations and reliance on external funding. BNP Paribas lowered its price target to $117 from $169 while retaining an ‘Outperform’ rating. MoffettNathanson cut its target to $89 from $107 and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating. The analysts highlighted the potential consequences of weaker investor confidence and expensive financing. CoreWeave needs capital to expand its data center infrastructure and support growing demand for computing capacity. Higher borrowing costs and limited access to capital markets could complicate its expansion plans and weigh on shareholder returns. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Eos Energy Enterprises stock touched a two-year low of $1.72 despite reporting preliminary third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $82 million to $83 million, a sequential growth of 19% to 21%. However, investors focused on the company’s expectation that 2026 revenue would land in the lower half of its previously announced $300 million to $350 million range. The updated outlook follows an earlier reduction in the company's revenue forecast in August. Eos has recorded eight consecutive quarters of improving gross margins, but its margins remain deeply negative as it works to increase production and improve manufacturing efficiency at its Thorn Hill facility. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’. So far this year, EYPT, CRWV and EOSE stocks have declined between 14% and 97%. After a steep climb driven by worry that global supply might tighten, the benchmark drifted lower as those fears eased and traders weighed the barrels flowing into the market. For a producer of this scale, softer crude trims the cash each barrel brings in, yet the effect is rarely uniform across the business. As crude eased, refining margins stayed firm, a detail that carried weight for the downstream arm. Refining spreads capture the gap between the cost of crude fed into a plant and the value of the fuels that emerge. When those spreads stay healthy even as crude softens, the refining side can lean into the difference. The company runs a meaningful refining and marketing operation, with plants able to process a range of crude grades and to tilt output toward the fuels in strongest demand. Firm margins there help steady group earnings when crude prices wobble. Exploration and production pull crude and natural gas from fields around the world. Refining and marketing turn those barrels into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. A chemicals arm converts hydrocarbons into the materials behind plastics and packaging. Each piece responds to its own set of drivers. The structure is built to smooth the swings. The upstream arm is the initial to feel any shift in crude. The company manages a broad spread of oil and gas fields, pairing mature assets that generate steady cash with newer developments meant to add fresh barrels. The portfolio reaches across shale, deepwater and large conventional fields, giving the production book exposure to many geographies. A softer crude price sharpens focus on the cost of each barrel. Producers that keep drilling and operating costs lean are better placed to keep cash moving when prices ease. Readers following Oil and Gas Stocks can place this update within its wider category. Among the company's growth engines, offshore developments in Guyana and shale acreage in the Permian basin stand out. The Permian, meanwhile, offers short-cycle shale wells that can be ramped or trimmed as prices move. The expansion of its stake in low-cost barrels has reshaped the company's production base, adding volumes that help offset decline elsewhere. Alongside these, the group carries assets spanning liquefied natural gas, offshore fields and conventional production, giving it reach across the full breadth of the oil and gas sector rather than exposure to any given region or grade of crude. Downstream and chemicals give the company levers beyond producing crude. Refining captures the spread between crude costs and fuel values, while chemicals turn hydrocarbons into resins and compounds for packaging, construction and consumer goods. Both arms move on rhythms that differ from the upstream business. With refining margins firm as crude eased, the downstream side provided a steadying counterweight. Chemicals follow their own cycle, tied to industrial activity and the cost of feedstock, and cheaper crude and gas can ease input costs for those plants. The wider energy sector moved together around the swing in crude. Oil and gas names tend to track the benchmark, rising when supply fears flare and easing when those fears fade. In that setting, the largest integrated names often serve as anchors. Their scale, diversified earnings and steady dividends give the market a reference point when crude churns. The energy cohort leaned on these heavyweight producers as traders weighed softer crude against firm refining margins, and the company stood among the most closely watched of them. The recent surge in crude traced to concern that global supply could tighten faster than new barrels could fill the gap. Geopolitics, disruptions and shifting plans among major exporters all feed that kind of unease, and prices tend to spike when scarcity dominates the conversation. The later easing reflected a calmer read on those same worries. For a group that both produces and refines, the swing is a lesson in balance. A sharp climb rewards production but pressures refining as feedstock costs rise. title: Why Did XOM, CVX, MPC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - TradingView
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. title: Better Oil Stock: Chevron (CVX) vs. ExxonMobil (XOM) - The Motley Fool
content: Which of these integrated energy giants is a better investment right now? Chevron (CVX +0.60%) and ExxonMobil (XOM -0.24%) are two of the world's largest integrated energy companies. They both own upstream exploration and extraction businesses, midstream pipelines, and downstream refineries. Over the past 12 months, Chevron's stock has rallied 45% while ExxonMobil's stock has risen 58%. Both stocks benefited from rising oil prices, but which stock is the better buy right now? Chevron is smaller than ExxonMobil, but both companies generate most of their revenue from their upstream businesses. However, Chevron generates more of its profits (about 80%) from its upstream business than ExxonMobil (about 70%). That's because ExxonMobil operates a larger downstream business -- which acts as a secondary profit engine -- than Chevron. ExxonMobil's downstream business produces a lot of petrochemicals, while Chevron's downstream business has minimal exposure to that market. When crude oil prices rise, upstream businesses typically grow their revenues faster than their expenses. However, downstream businesses often struggle as their input costs rise. When crude oil prices decline, upstream businesses struggle, but downstream businesses fare better -- as long as the crack spread (between crude oil costs and retail fuel prices) remains stable. Therefore, Chevron's streamlined, upstream-heavy business model makes it a more attractive investment than ExxonMobil when oil prices spike. But when oil prices pull back, ExxonMobil's scale and downstream diversification could make it a more compelling investment. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you’d invested $5,000 then, you’d be sitting on $2,821,947 today.* Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It’s a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. However, the price of Brent crude oil -- currently at $110 per barrel -- remains far above ExxonMobil's breakeven price (for covering capex and dividends) of $35 per barrel and Chevron's breakeven price of $50 per barrel. Both companies plan to increase their oil and gas production by about 3% annually through the end of the decade. Chevron pays a forward yield of 3.2%, while ExxonMobil pays a lower forward yield of 2.3%. Chevron has raised its dividend annually for 39 consecutive years, while ExxonMobil has maintained that streak for 43 years. If they reach 50 years, they'll become Dividend Kings. Both companies have plenty of room to raise their dividends. Over the past 12 months, Chevron and ExxonMobil had payout ratios of 67% and 53%, respectively. In 2025, Chevron's EPS dropped 32% as crude oil prices declined, its refining margins shrank, and it finalized its acquisition of Hess Corporation. But from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect its EPS to grow at a 26% CAGR as it expands in Guyana (one of the world's fastest-growing oil regions) by integrating Hess' assets; produces more oil in the Permian Basin and Kazakhstan, and accelerates its deepwater projects. Yet its stock still trades at 15 times next year's earnings. In 2025, ExxonMobil's EPS dipped 15% as it faced some of the same headwinds as Chevron and divested its weaker assets. But from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect its EPS to grow at a 20% CAGR as it integrates its recent acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources (which expanded its reach in the Permian Basin), increases its production in Guyana, and prioritizes the production of higher-margin chemical performance products and specialized fuels at its downstream business. Its stock also trades at 15 times next year's earnings. Chevron and ExxonMobil both look fundamentally cheap because they're valued as cyclical commodity stocks rather than higher-growth energy plays. However, Chevron generates more of its profits (about 80%) from its upstream business than ExxonMobil (about 70%). That's because ExxonMobil operates a larger downstream business -- which acts as a secondary profit engine -- than Chevron. ExxonMobil's downstream business produces a lot of petrochemicals, while Chevron's downstream business has minimal exposure to that market. When crude oil prices rise, upstream businesses typically grow their revenues faster than their expenses. However, downstream businesses often struggle as their input costs rise. When crude oil prices decline, upstream businesses struggle, but downstream businesses fare better -- as long as the crack spread (between crude oil costs and retail fuel prices) remains stable. Therefore, Chevron's streamlined, upstream-heavy business model makes it a more attractive investment than ExxonMobil when oil prices spike. But when oil prices pull back, ExxonMobil's scale and downstream diversification could make it a more compelling investment. Its stock also trades at 15 times next year's earnings. title: Is Chevron Stock Worth More Than Its Competitors? - Trefis
content: Chevron (CVX) stock currently trades at 21.5 times earnings, giving it the second-highest P/E among a peer group of six oil and gas companies. Yet the stock recorded the smallest gain in that group after rising 53.7% over the year to October 16, 2026. Three refiners in the same peer group saw their shares more than double during that period. So what does Chevron deliver for a price near the top of its group? Across the four fiscal quarters that ended June 30, 2026, Chevron outperformed Exxon Mobil, the only other integrated oil and gas company in the group. Chevron reported revenue growth of 11.2%, compared to 9.6% at Exxon Mobil. The company also kept 12.4% of its sales as operating profit, whereas its rival retained 10.7%. Despite trailing in these metrics, Exxon Mobil commands a higher valuation at 22.8 times earnings. Comparisons with the rest of the peer group depend on the underlying business. The operators that refine and sell fuel include Marathon Petroleum, Phillips 66 and Valero Energy. All three grew faster than Chevron and trade at lower P/Es, yet none kept more than 7.5% of its sales as operating profit. ConocoPhillips, an exploration and production company, earned the widest margin in the group at 21.9%. It trades at a lower P/E than Chevron while growing more slowly. When measured against its single direct competitor running the same integrated business model, Chevron delivers stronger results for slightly less money. The timing of Chevron’s operating profit reveals a heavy tilt toward the final period. Out of a total $25.8 billion generated over those four quarters, $14.3 billion arrived in the single quarter that ended June 30, 2026. Chevron recorded an operating margin of 21% in that specific period, up from 9.1% a year earlier. Across each of the three preceding quarters, that margin stayed below 9%. Chevron operates two primary segments. Its Upstream segment produces the oil and gas, while its Downstream segment refines and sells fuel. During a July 31, 2026 call, management said adjusted earnings from producing oil and gas rose on higher prices, higher volumes and favorable timing effects. In the refining business, management stated that adjusted earnings rose mainly on higher refining margins and favorable timing effects. Chevron has also lowered its costs. Management said the company cut $3 billion of costs over the twelve months before the call, ahead of schedule. Management’s targets for 2030 project steady growth. These targets are set at flat oil and gas prices, which sit below those recorded at the time of its July call. On the July 31, 2026 call, management said it still expects Chevron’s production to grow 2% to 3% a year. The company also expects adjusted free cash flow, its own measure of cash left after investment, to grow by more than 10% a year on average. The market currently values Chevron at a P/E near the top of its group, a multiple measured on four quarters of earnings that include the June quarter. So far, the June quarter stands as the only recent period in which Chevron earned a margin that wide. Operating margin remains the key metric to watch in the company’s next report, expected on or around October 30, 2026. Not necessarily on Chevron alone, if your goal is long-term wealth. title: CVX Stock Rises Overnight: Chevron Says It Has Discovered Oil, Gas Condensate Offshore In Angola - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Chevron Corp. (CVX) closed up more than 1% on Monday and continued to climb in the overnight session. The company said that it had made an oil and gas condensate discovery at the 105-4X exploration well in Block 0, offshore Angola. The discovery will aid its ‌push to increase production in sub-Saharan Africa and demonstrates the potential of its exploration program in the region, the company said. The company said that the well, drilled in the prolific Lower Congo Basin, found an oil and gas condensate column of more than 600 meters (2,000 feet) in the primary Pinda reservoir. Chevron plans to assess the asset for potential development as a tie-back to its nearby facilities. The company said that beyond Angola, the discovery builds on a successful exploration program in Sub-Saharan Africa where Chevron is currently producing around 300 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day net. Its existing resource base and active exploration program across the region is positioned to sustain and grow production into the future. “This discovery is another important milestone for Chevron’s over 70-year history in Angola,” said Kevin McLachlan, Vice President, Exploration, Chevron. “By combining high-impact exploration with infrastructure-led opportunities close to existing facilities, we are growing our resource base, creating value, and demonstrating that our strategy is delivering, as well as our continued confidence in Angola’s resource potential.” In Nigeria, Chevron farmed into two offshore blocks last year and has also been awarded a deepwater block in the country's latest bid round. Chevron has also had three near-field exploration successes – Meji NW-1, South Delta AA and Awodi-07 – in Nigeria since late 2024, where it is continuing an ongoing exploration and appraisal program. In Guinea-Bissau, Chevron has secured three blocks, including the newly acquired Block 4B, which closed on Aug. 13th; in Equatorial Guinea, it has secured an additional five-block reconnaissance license. Barclays lowered the price target on Chevron to $208 from $216 and maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating on the shares, as per TheFly. The revised target still implies an upside of about 2.6% from the company’s last closing price. The firm said it adjusted targets in the integrated oil and exploration and product group after its second-quarter earnings. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) broke a two-day losing streak on Monday as the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) weighed Ligado Networks’ application to beam L-band broadband from 96 satellites in AST’s constellation. ASTS stock ended 0.2% higher on Monday after declining over 4% in the previous two sessions. Ligado filed the request in December, and the FCC accepted it for filing on Jan. 30, 2026. FCC records still list the application as “Pending Review,” with no grant date. Approval could give AST a dedicated satellite-spectrum layer alongside the terrestrial frequencies supplied by partners including AT&T, Verizon and FirstNet. Ligado wants to modify its existing SkyTerra-1 license to add a low-Earth-orbit Mobile Satellite Service network called SkyTerra Next. According to its technical supplement, Ligado-controlled L-band payloads would operate aboard 96 AST satellites at an altitude of roughly 690 kilometers. The system’s steerable beams and variable power controls can mitigate interference, while Ligado would retain the ability to shut down particular frequencies or beams. AST would provide the satellites and supporting infrastructure. In a December letter, the company said the partnership would deliver space-based broadband to U.S. subscribers through their “existing, unmodified mobile devices.” Ligado also asked the FCC to waive rules that generally place new non-geostationary systems into processing rounds with competing applicants. The company said that SkyTerra Next would use its previously coordinated L-band spectrum rather than seek new frequencies. Requiring another round, Ligado said, would cause delays and “stifle the innovative new technology” enabled by its AST partnership. After the FCC opened the application to public responses in January, opponents raised concerns about interference involving GPS, aviation, weather and satellite communications systems. They also questioned whether the proposal was effectively a new NGSO network or a transfer of license control to AST. However, Ligado and AST rejected the claims, maintaining that Ligado would retain ownership and operational control. After additional technical questions submitted in May, Ligado responded with analyses conducted with AST and outside consultants, which showed that the system would fit within existing authorizations without causing harmful interference. Ligado said the narrower LEO beams would reduce unintended coverage of sensitive facilities and pledged to “promptly resolve” any interference. The filing supports an agreement giving AST more than 80 years of usage rights to as much as 45 MHz of spectrum, including up to 40 MHz of Ligado’s L-band holdings. The deal includes a $550 million payment from AST upon regulatory closing and minimum annual L-band payments of about $80 million. A bankruptcy court approved the deal in June last year and confirmed Ligado’s reorganization plan in September 2025. Tesla has reportedly told staff it is preparing a public launch of the Cybercab—its first vehicle without a steering wheel or brake pedal—for its Robotaxi autonomous ride-hailing service, potentially as soon as this month in Austin, Texas. The Information reported the company’s plans, citing people familiar with the matter. Tesla’s regulatory status for commercial Cybercab service, however, is unclear, the report noted. The two-seat Cybercab is designed for driverless operation. Tesla has tested Cybercabs on public roads nationwide since June but limited rides to internal use. In July, it began offering employees rides on private roads near its Austin campus and gathering feedback, mirroring steps it took before launching its first Robotaxi hub there last year. According to The Information, staff were informed that the public phase would begin with Cybercab rides for Tesla employees on public roads, and that the vehicles would be integrated into the existing Austin Robotaxi service within days. The internal target is the end of August, though it could shift amid ongoing preparations, the report said. Tesla completed emergency training with Austin first responders last week on handling the vehicles, including moving them if needed, the report added. Tesla currently runs its Austin Robotaxi service with about 186 registered Model Y vehicles. It remains unclear whether Cybercabs will replace or supplement that fleet. The company has remote operators who can monitor and take control in emergencies. In its second-quarter 2026 update and earnings call last month, Tesla said it has started production of the Cybercab at Gigafactory Texas. The company listed installed annual manufacturing capacity exceeding 125,000 units. CEO Elon Musk noted during the company’s earnings call that the Cybercab’s new chassis requires specific data before broader deployment: “We need to accumulate driving data that is specific to the Cybercab before we can put a lot of them on the road.” Tesla is gathering miles using units retrofitted with steering wheels and pedals for calibration. AI executive Ashok Elluswamy called it “a phenomenal product” that riders “instantly fall in love with,” adding that manufacturing targets align with unsupervised Robotaxi mile growth. Cybercab is central to shifting Tesla away from merely an EV maker to autonomous driving and robotics. The company expects to spend more than $25 billion this year on supporting the transition, roughly three times its 2025 capital expenditure of $8.5 billion.
